newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 14.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Philippine Central Bank is investigating local banks which had been buying dollars heavily in recent days to check whether they were the ones leading the speculative attacks on the peso, bank governor Gabriel Singson said. (TODAY)

- President Fidel Ramos appealed for calm on Sunday as fears of higher prices and hoarding swept the country following the peso's 11.5 percent drop to 29.45 per dollar. (INQUIRER, MALAYA, PHILIPPINE STAR, MANILA TIMES)
- Manila has awarded a $500-million contract to the Philippine International Air Terminals Co Inc for the construction of another terminal at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- The Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co is expected to generate some 7.9 billion pesos in additional revenues annually once it starts metering phone calls, according to an economist at the University of Asia and the Pacific. (MALAYA)
- Thailand's currency and short-term economic problems could intensify following the Philippine peso's de facto devaluation last Friday, analysts said. (BUSINESSWORLD)

- The de facto devaluation of the peso would affect the financial performance of state-controlled National Power Corp. Napocor vice president for finance Merlita Pajarillo said that every one peso drop in the exchange rate of the peso against the dollar meant an increase of 300 million pesos in the power firm's 10.5-billion peso debt to multilateral creditors. (MANILA STANDARD)

- The Department of Trade and Industry is bracing itself for unusual surges in prices of basic commodities and goods following a Monetary Board decision to allow the peso to fluctuate within a wider band against the dollar. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Computer dealers in Manila raised prices of personal computers by five to 10 percent starting on Saturday, a day after the peso plunged by 11.5 percent to 29.45. (MANILA TIMES)
